However, the fate of kinetic constraints in the weakly dissipative limit remains unexplored in large systems above one dimension. To access large system sizes and two-dimensional geometries, we employ the truncated Wigner approximation, a phase-space method that captures correlated many-body dynamics beyond classical rate equations. To probe the emergence of kinetic constraints on timescales where coherent and dissipative processes are comparable, we analyse the relaxation dynamics starting from two initial states: a fully polarised state and a Néel state, which belongs to a manifold of so-called quantum scars. In both cases, we observe a pronounced slowdown in the relaxation of the magnetisation towards the stationary state and identify transient signatures of quantum kinetically constrained dynamics in one and two dimensions.
tldr: This paper studies the relaxation dynamics of a dissipative Rydberg gas, revealing quantum kinetically constrained behavior in the weakly dissipative limit.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints from the Rydberg blockade affect relaxation dynamics when coherent and dissipative processes compete, especially in large systems and 2D geometries.
method: The authors use the truncated Wigner approximation, a phase-space method, to simulate the many-body dynamics beyond classical rate equations, analyzing relaxation from polarized and Néel states.
result: They observe a pronounced slowdown in magnetization relaxation and identify transient signatures of quantum kinetically constrained dynamics in both 1D and 2D.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of kinetically constrained dynamics to the weakly dissipative regime, showing quantum effects beyond classical descriptions.

title: Spin-based True Random Number Generation Enabled By Voltage-amplified Quantum Fluctuations
authors: Jie Zheng, Jiyong Kang, Zheng Zhu, Di Wu, Yuesheng Li, Dongxing Yu, Jiayong Wang, Hongxing Xu And Chenglong Jia
abstract: We investigate spin quantum-fluctuation effects that originate from the Heisenberg uncertainty principle during the dynamical cycle of disentanglement, entanglement, and re-disentanglement between itinerant electrons and localized magnetic moments mediated by the s–d exchange interaction. Beyond conventional deterministic spin-transfer torque, we analyze an intrinsic mechanism that transfers spin quantum fluctuations to a nanomagnet. By extending the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation to incorporate both quantum and thermal stochastic fields, we identify a temperature regime in which quantum fluctuations dominate the magnetization dynamics. We further show that voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy exponentially amplifies spin quantum fluctuations, enabling binary readout through magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions. These findings provide a microscopic framework for fluctuation-driven spin dynamics and outline a device-level pathway toward spin-based quantum true random number generation.
tldr: This paper proposes a spin-based true random number generator exploiting voltage-amplified quantum fluctuations in magnetization dynamics.
motivation: To provide a microscopic framework for fluctuation-driven spin dynamics and a device-level pathway for quantum true random number generation.
method: Extends the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation with quantum and thermal stochastic fields, and analyzes voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy to amplify spin quantum fluctuations.
result: Identifies a temperature regime where quantum fluctuations dominate, and shows that voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy exponentially amplifies these fluctuations, enabling binary readout via magnetoresistance.
conclusion: The findings offer a device-level approach to spin-based quantum true random number generation, leveraging quantum fluctuations in nanomagnets.

title: Sparse Identification Of Quantum Hamiltonian Dynamics Via Quantum Circuit Learning
authors: Yusei Tateyama And Yuzuru Kato
abstract: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy) is a data-driven framework for estimating classical nonlinear dynamical systems from time-series data. In this approach, system dynamics is represented as a linear combination of a predefined set of basis functions, and the corresponding coefficients are sparsely estimated from observed time-series data. In this study, we propose sparse identification of quantum Hamiltonian dynamics (SIQHDy), a SINDy-inspired quantum circuit learning framework for estimating quantum Hamiltonian dynamics from time-series data of quantum measurement outcomes. In SIQHDy, the unitary evolution of a quantum Hamiltonian system is expressed as a product of basis quantum circuits, and the corresponding circuit parameters are estimated through sparsity-promoting optimization. We numerically demonstrate that SIQHDy accurately reconstructs the dynamics of single-, three-, and five-spin systems, and exhibits robustness to measurement noise in the three-spin case. Furthermore, we propose an extension of SIQHDy for scenarios with limited accessible observables and evaluate its performance in identifying three-spin systems and in network-structure identification for five-spin systems.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum circuit learning framework inspired by SINDy to sparsely identify quantum Hamiltonian dynamics from measurement time-series data.
motivation: Estimating quantum Hamiltonian dynamics from data is crucial for characterizing quantum systems, but existing methods may require many measurements or prior knowledge. The authors aim to provide a data-driven approach that leverages sparsity to efficiently reconstruct the dynamics.
method: The method, SIQHDy, represents the unitary evolution as a product of basis quantum circuits and estimates the circuit parameters via sparsity-promoting optimization, using time-series data of quantum measurement outcomes. An extension handles limited accessible observables.
result: Numerical demonstrations show accurate reconstruction for single-, three-, and five-spin systems, with robustness to measurement noise in the three-spin case. The extension also performs well in identifying three-spin systems and network structures for five-spin systems.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a promising data-driven tool for quantum Hamiltonian identification, with potential applications in quantum system characterization and quantum network inference.

title: Rotation-enhanced Photonic Spin Hall Effect In A Ring Bose–Einstein Condensate
authors: Leibo Deng, Muqaddar Abbas, Ghaisud Din, Hocine Bahlouli And Yong-Hong Ma
abstract: We show that rotation can strongly amplify the photonic spin Hall effect in a ring Bose–Einstein condensate. For an incident probe beam carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM), the spin-dependent transverse shift of the reflected light is weak in the non-rotating regime but becomes strongly enhanced under rotation because rotation lifts the degeneracy of the condensate mechanical modes via Bragg scattering. The resulting mode splitting produces large photonic spin Hall shifts at ultra-low optical power, with the enhancement increasing with both the condensate winding number and the probe OAM , while remaining weakly affected by atom–atom interactions. Our findings elucidate a rotation-governed mechanism underlying spin-dependent light transport in hybrid atom–optomechanical systems, thereby highlighting its potential for applications in high-precision rotational sensing.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that rotation can strongly enhance the photonic spin Hall effect in a ring Bose-Einstein condensate, enabling large spin-dependent shifts at ultra-low optical power.
motivation: The photonic spin Hall effect is typically weak, and the authors seek a mechanism to amplify it for applications in precision sensing. They explore a hybrid atom-optomechanical system where rotation lifts degeneracy and enhances the effect.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a ring Bose-Einstein condensate coupled to an optical cavity, considering Bragg scattering and mechanical mode splitting induced by rotation. They derive expressions for the spin-dependent transverse shift of reflected light as a function of rotation, winding number, and probe OAM.
result: Rotation strongly enhances the photonic spin Hall shift, with the enhancement increasing with condensate winding number and probe OAM, while being weakly affected by atom-atom interactions. The effect occurs at ultra-low optical power.
conclusion: The findings reveal a rotation-governed mechanism for spin-dependent light transport in hybrid atom-optomechanical systems, with potential for high-precision rotational sensing.

title: Exact Quantum Many-Body Scars In 2d Quantum Gauge Models
authors: Yuan Miao, Linhao Li, Hosho Katsura, And Masahito Yamazaki
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2164 (2026).

Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) serve as important examples of ergodicity-breaking phenomena in quantum many-body systems. Despite recent extensive studies, exact QMBS are rare in dimensions higher than one. In this paper, we study a two-dimensional quantum [MATH] gauge model that is dual to a two-dimensional spin-[MATH] XY model defined on bipartite graphs. We identify the exact eigenstates of the XY model with a tower structure as exact QMBS. Exploiting the duality transformation, we show that the exact QMBS of the XY model (and XXZ model) after the transformation are the exact QMBS of the dual [MATH] gauge model. This construction is versatile and has potential applications for finding new QMBS in other higher-dimensional models.

.
tldr: This paper constructs exact quantum many-body scars in a 2D quantum gauge model via duality to an XY model, providing a new example of ergodicity breaking in higher dimensions.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) are rare in dimensions higher than one, and this work aims to find exact QMBS in a 2D gauge model, which is relevant to understanding ergodicity breaking in quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors study a 2D quantum gauge model dual to a 2D spin-1/2 XY model on bipartite graphs, identify exact eigenstates with a tower structure in the XY model, and use the duality transformation to map them to exact QMBS in the gauge model.
result: They demonstrate that the exact QMBS of the XY and XXZ models become exact QMBS of the dual gauge model, providing a versatile construction for finding QMBS in higher-dimensional models.
conclusion: The work offers a new method to construct exact QMBS in higher dimensions, potentially advancing the study of ergodicity breaking and non-thermal behavior in quantum many-body systems.

title: Entropic Collapse And Extreme First-passage Times In Discrete Ballistic Transport
authors: Bhargav R Karamched
abstract: We investigate the extreme first-passage statistics of non-interacting random walkers on hierarchical ballistic graphs. By distinguishing between transport limited by escape from localized initial states (injection-limited) and transport limited by the extended network (bulk-limited), we identify a class of extreme value statistics that arises in geometries dominated by source traps (e.g. the Comet graph). In this regime, the distribution of the minimum arrival time does not converge to any of the classical generalized extreme value distributions. Instead, it follows a discrete distribution with a strict lower time bound determined by the properties of the hierarchical network. We analytically derive the asymptotic behavior of this class and validate our predictions against Monte Carlo simulations. Crucially, we identify the mechanism of ‘entropic collapse’ that destroys this scaling in bulk-dominated geometries like the Bethe lattice, where the phase space of delayed paths diverges with distance. This work establishes a geometry-encoding function that acts as a diagnostic tool for ascertaining whether or not a given graph is hierarchical.
tldr: This paper studies extreme first-passage statistics of random walkers on hierarchical ballistic graphs, identifying a new class of extreme value statistics and the mechanism of 'entropic collapse'.
motivation: To understand extreme first-passage times in complex networks, which is relevant to transport phenomena but not directly to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
method: The authors analytically derive asymptotic behavior for a class of extreme value statistics on hierarchical graphs, distinguishing injection-limited and bulk-limited transport, and validate with Monte Carlo simulations.
result: They find a discrete distribution for minimum arrival times in source-trap geometries, and identify 'entropic collapse' that destroys scaling in bulk-dominated geometries, establishing a geometry-encoding function.
conclusion: The work provides a diagnostic tool for identifying hierarchical graphs, but it is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dimensionality And Confinement Reshape Competition In Cellular Renewing Active Matter
authors: Philip Bittihn And Yoav G Pollack Patrick Zimmer
abstract: Cellular renewing active matter—assemblies of proliferating and apoptotic cells—underlies tissue homeostasis, morphogenesis, and clonal competition. Previous work in one-dimensional periodic systems identified a fitness advantage associated with rapid dead-cell clearance, an ‘opportunistic’ competition mechanism. Extending this framework, we study two-dimensional cellular aggregates and show that dimensionality modifies the interplay between competition mechanisms for clones with different clearance rates: in 2D, opportunistic and homeostatic-pressure-based competition jointly shape clonal selection, to varying degrees. We then introduce an explicit circular confinement to probe how physical boundaries modulate this interplay. While opportunistic competition persists, distinct time-dependent behaviors emerge through weakened homeostatic-pressure-based competition near boundaries. Structural analysis reveals that confinement promotes tangential alignment and spatially heterogeneous homeostatic pressure, thereby reshaping competitive outcomes at tissue edges. Partial information decomposition allows us to attribute these differing outcomes to temporally and spatially varying relative contributions of the two mechanisms. Our study connects newly discovered competition mechanisms with more realistic biological contexts, highlighting how dimensionality and spatial constraints influence tissue structures and modulate competition in heterogeneous cell populations across time and space, with implications for tumor growth dynamics and tissue development.
tldr: This paper studies cellular renewing active matter in 2D with confinement, focusing on clonal competition mechanisms, which is outside the user's research interests.
motivation: To understand how dimensionality and spatial constraints affect competition in cellular aggregates, with implications for tissue development and tumor growth.
method: Extends a 1D model to 2D, introduces circular confinement, and uses partial information decomposition to analyze competition mechanisms.
result: Dimensionality and confinement alter the interplay between opportunistic and homeostatic-pressure-based competition, with boundary effects leading to spatially heterogeneous outcomes.
conclusion: The study connects competition mechanisms to realistic biological contexts, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Excitons In 2H-MoTe2: Anisotropies, Masses And Binding Energy
authors: Zahra Ahmadi Heidari And Martin Knupfer
abstract: Bound electron–hole pairs called excitons determine the photophysical behavior of semiconducting materials. In this study, we present a combination of electron energy-loss spectroscopy in transmission and optical absorption spectroscopy for the investigation of excitons in bulk 2H-MoTe2. The exciton dispersion E(q) was measured for momentum transfers oriented along the ΓK and ΓM directions at 20 K. From the extracted dispersion relations, the in-plane exciton effective mass was determined. Our results reveal that for 2H-MoTe2 the exciton effective mass is anisotropic. In consideration of the complementary optical results the exciton reduced mass, binding energy and radius have been determined.
tldr: This paper studies exciton properties in bulk 2H-MoTe2 using electron energy-loss spectroscopy and optical absorption, focusing on anisotropic effective masses and binding energy.
motivation: Understanding exciton behavior in transition metal dichalcogenides is important for optoelectronic applications, but this work is purely experimental materials characterization without a quantum information or thermodynamics angle.
method: The authors combine electron energy-loss spectroscopy in transmission and optical absorption spectroscopy to measure exciton dispersion along ΓK and ΓM directions at 20 K, extracting effective masses and binding parameters.
result: They find that the exciton effective mass is anisotropic in the plane, and determine the reduced mass, binding energy, and radius.
conclusion: The study provides detailed exciton parameters for 2H-MoTe2, but it does not connect to quantum information processing or thermodynamics.

title: Low-dimensional Dynamical Behavior Of Locally Coupled Chiral Swarmalators
authors: Zihan Li, Yonggang Wu, Xiaoyu Zhang, Zhigang Zheng And Duxin Chen
abstract: Understanding the dynamical behavior of swarmalators, particularly the transition from disorder to synchronization, constitutes one of the pivotal frontiers in the study of complex systems. We propose an ansatz that successfully decouples the spatial and phase dynamics in the locally coupled chiral swarmalators model, enabling rigorous analytical treatment of this complex system. Within this framework, we systematically examine how the interaction radius affects system synchronization, quantified through an order parameter measuring phase coherence. Our theoretical analysis reveals that increasing the interaction radius enhances synchronization in both velocity and phase dynamics. This relationship demonstrates that larger interaction networks facilitate more efficient information transfer among heterogeneous oscillators with different intrinsic frequencies. Using a self-consistent approach in the thermodynamic limit, we derive analytical expressions for the order parameter that accurately predict the synchronization transition. These findings provide fundamental insights into synchronization mechanisms in spatially embedded swarmalator systems with applications in understanding biological collective behaviors.
tldr: This paper analyzes synchronization in a model of chiral swarmalators with local coupling, deriving analytical expressions for the order parameter.
motivation: Understanding synchronization in spatially embedded oscillator systems is important for biological collective behaviors, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors propose an ansatz to decouple spatial and phase dynamics, then use a self-consistent approach in the thermodynamic limit to derive analytical expressions for the order parameter.
result: They find that increasing interaction radius enhances synchronization in both velocity and phase dynamics, and their analytical predictions match the transition.
conclusion: The work provides insights into synchronization mechanisms in swarmalator systems, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: Bridging Scales: From Classical Colloidal Crystals To Mesocrystals With Modern X-ray Synchrotron Methods
authors: Janne-Mieke Meijer, Elena V Sturm, Andrei V Petukhov And Ivan A Vartanyants
abstract: This review explores different colloidal systems and their crystals as well as their special case namely—mesocrystals. First, we highlight recent advances in fabrication methods of colloidal crystals (mesocrystals) and then describe small-angle and ultra-small-angle x-ray scattering from colloidal assemblies organized from particles of different shape. Here, we already introduce different types of defects that are present in colloidal crystals. Next, we go to a modern description of angular x-ray cross-correlation analysis and its applications on colloidal and mesocrystalline materials. After that we discuss phase retrieval techniques, namely coherent x-ray diffraction imaging and ptychography, as emerging tools for structural characterization of colloidal crystals and mesocrystals. We conclude with perspectives on the opportunities that will be provided by the 4th generation synchrotron sources for studying colloidal crystals and mesocrystals.
tldr: This review covers colloidal crystals and mesocrystals, focusing on X-ray scattering and imaging techniques, which are not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to review recent advances in fabricating and characterizing colloidal crystals and mesocrystals using modern synchrotron X-ray methods.
method: It reviews small-angle and ultra-small-angle X-ray scattering, angular X-ray cross-correlation analysis, and coherent X-ray diffraction imaging and ptychography.
result: The review highlights the capabilities of these techniques for structural characterization and discusses future opportunities with 4th generation synchrotron sources.
conclusion: The paper concludes that these advanced X-ray methods will enable deeper understanding of colloidal and mesocrystalline structures.

title: The Paradox Of Steady-state Light Diffusion
authors: André Liemert, Lorenzo Pattelli, Alwin Kienle, Federico Tommasi And Fabrizio Martelli
abstract: For over thirty years, the definition of the diffusion coefficient in light transport has been the subject of persistent debate. Its canonical expression includes an explicit dependence on absorption, violating a fundamental scaling property of the radiative transfer equation (RTE). In the time domain (TD), evidence shows that the correct definition is independent of absorption, yet absorption-dependent formulations unfortunately remain common in practical data analysis. In the continuous-wave regime, the radial decay of the RTE can be reproduced by an absorption-dependent coefficient, but this does not imply that steady-state transport is genuinely diffusive. Here, this controversy is resolved through an exact consistency test based solely on the requirement that diffusion converges to the RTE in the limit of infinite propagation. In the TD, we prove that the absorption-independent coefficient is both necessary and sufficient for exact long-time convergence. In the continuous-wave regime, we prove analytically that no scalar diffusion coefficient can make diffusion asymptotically equivalent to the RTE when absorption is nonzero: matching the dominant attenuation length fixes one coefficient, whereas matching the residue requires a different one. We further show that this failure is not caused by any finite set of ballistic or few-scattering contributions, and quantify the intrinsic error introduced by incorrect parameterizations in idealized absorption-retrieval scenarios. These results establish the time-domain formulation as the only self-consistent reference and call for a re-examination of how diffusion is applied in optical transport studies.
tldr: This paper resolves the long-standing debate on the diffusion coefficient in light transport, proving that in steady-state with absorption no scalar diffusion coefficient can asymptotically match the radiative transfer equation.
motivation: The definition of the diffusion coefficient in light transport has been debated for decades, with absorption-dependent formulations violating scaling properties of the RTE. The authors aim to resolve this controversy through an exact consistency test.
method: The authors use analytical proofs and exact consistency tests based on the requirement that diffusion converges to the RTE in the limit of infinite propagation, analyzing both time-domain and continuous-wave regimes.
result: They prove that in the time domain, an absorption-independent coefficient is necessary and sufficient for exact long-time convergence, while in the continuous-wave regime with nonzero absorption, no scalar diffusion coefficient can make diffusion asymptotically equivalent to the RTE.
conclusion: The time-domain formulation is established as the only self-consistent reference, calling for re-examination of diffusion applications in optical transport studies.

title: Emergent Symmetry-protected Topological Phases Via Polyakov Confinement In Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Shun-Li Yu And Jian-Xin Li Li-Wei He
abstract: A main theme in modern condensed matter physics is the emergence of fractionalized excitations and gauge structures from quantum spin systems. However, understanding how these exotic degrees of freedom reconfine into new phases of matter remains a fundamental challenge. In this work, we demonstrate that Polyakov’s confinement mechanism-a foundation of compact gauge theory-can serve as a dynamical engine to transform a Dirac spin liquid (DSL) into a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) state. Starting with a DSL with spin-dependent gauge fluxes, we show that the single-occupancy constraint inherent to the physical Hilbert space triggers monopole condensation, dynamically confining bulk spinons while preserving gapless edge modes-realizing a spinon analog of the quantum spin Hall effect. Using a large-scale variational Monte Carlo simulation on a triangular antiferromagnet with an additional Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, we provide microscopic evidence for this confined SPT phase, including a characteristic area law for the Wilson loop and vanishing topological entanglement entropy. Furthermore, we identify a measurable spin-pump response under magnetic fields, which directly encodes the Berry curvature of the parent Dirac cones. Our results reveal a previously unexplored pathway to SPT physics, bridging the fields of gauge theory, quantum magnetism, and topological matter.
tldr: This paper uses Polyakov confinement to transform a Dirac spin liquid into a symmetry-protected topological state in a quantum spin system, with variational Monte Carlo evidence.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how fractionalized excitations reconfine into new phases of matter, specifically exploring a mechanism to generate SPT phases from a DSL.
method: They employ large-scale variational Monte Carlo simulations on a triangular antiferromagnet with Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, analyzing Wilson loops and topological entanglement entropy.
result: They find a confined SPT phase with area-law Wilson loop and vanishing topological entanglement entropy, and identify a spin-pump response encoding Berry curvature.
conclusion: The work reveals a new pathway to SPT physics, bridging gauge theory, quantum magnetism, and topological matter, but is primarily a condensed matter physics result.

title: Tailoring Reflectionless Complex Media For non-Abelian Braiding Of Acoustic Modes
authors: Hongkuan Zhang And Guancong Ma
abstract: Multiple scattering of sound and light can be tailored for diverse applications. Despite the great progress enabled by technologies such as time-reversal propagation and wavefront shaping, the full control of the transmission matrix remains a significant challenge. In this work, we propose a multi-scattering-based approach to design reflectionless complex media with an arbitrary unitary transmission matrix. As such, the perfect transmission of waves through such a medium performs a unitary operation. Based on this principle, we experimentally demonstrated braiding of multiple waveguide modes in an acoustic waveguide via multiple scattering and showed non-Abelian characteristics arising from the concatenation of distinct complex media. Furthermore, we show that the principle can be extended for realizing arbitrary unitary operations beyond braiding. Our scheme uses generalized Wigner–Smith operators to design the optimal acoustic complex media with near-arbitrary targeted functionalities. The scheme is generally applicable beyond acoustics, with broad implications to other wave types. Our results demonstrate unprecedented control over multiple-scattering waves and establish complex media as a viable route to modal control and operations on compact platforms, providing a new design paradigm for multimode, reconfigurable wave-based devices with potential applications in multiplexed communication, imaging, and the manipulation of quantum waves.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to design reflectionless complex media with arbitrary unitary transmission matrices, experimentally demonstrating non-Abelian braiding of acoustic modes.
motivation: The authors aim to achieve full control of the transmission matrix in multiple-scattering systems, which is a significant challenge, and to explore non-Abelian operations for wave-based devices.
method: They use generalized Wigner-Smith operators to design acoustic complex media that realize arbitrary unitary transmission matrices, and experimentally demonstrate braiding of waveguide modes in an acoustic waveguide.
result: They experimentally show non-Abelian characteristics from concatenating distinct complex media and extend the principle to arbitrary unitary operations beyond braiding.
conclusion: The scheme provides a new design paradigm for multimode, reconfigurable wave-based devices with potential applications in communication, imaging, and quantum wave manipulation, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests.

title: Moiré-driven Skyrmion Family
authors: Kuan He, Meng-Han Li, Shi-Da Fan, Zi-Bin Lin, Xiao-Ying Zhuang, Cheng-Lin Han, Li-Qun Chen, Zhao-Dong Xu, Xue-Feng Zhu And Tian-Zhi Yang
abstract: Skyrmion family members, including skyrmions, merons, and skyrmioniums, have been observed in diverse physical systems, yet their coexistence and transformation within a single controllable platform remain challenging. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a bilayer twisted moiré elastic system that enables the generation of multiple skyrmion family members with different topological charges. By constructing three-dimensional displacement vector fields, we establish a framework describing the evolution of topological invariants under twist-induced symmetry modulation, thereby governing controlled transitions and the stable coexistence of different skyrmion textures. In addition, manipulating the Lamb-wave phase introduces discontinuous transport of the topological textures, thereby revealing phason-like dynamics within the quasiperiodic structure. Together, these results provide a versatile route for controlling topological textures and open new possibilities for the design of integrated topological wave devices.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a moiré-driven elastic system that generates and controls skyrmion family members, focusing on topological textures in mechanical metamaterials.
motivation: The authors aim to achieve coexistence and transformation of multiple skyrmion family members in a single controllable platform, which has been challenging in diverse physical systems.
method: They construct a bilayer twisted moiré elastic system and use three-dimensional displacement vector fields to describe topological invariant evolution under twist-induced symmetry modulation, also manipulating Lamb-wave phase for discontinuous transport.
result: They experimentally demonstrate generation of multiple skyrmion family members with different topological charges and controlled transitions, revealing phason-like dynamics in the quasiperiodic structure.
conclusion: The work provides a versatile route for controlling topological textures and opens possibilities for integrated topological wave devices.

title: Probing Quark Electromagnetic Properties Via Entangled Quark Pairs In Fragmentation Hadrons At Lepton Colliders
authors: Qing-Hong Cao, Guanghui Li, Xin-Kai Wen And Bin Yan
abstract: Electromagnetic dipole interactions of light quarks induce distinct spin correlations in quark pairs produced at lepton colliders, favoring entangled spin-triplet state aligned along the axis or spin-singlet state. These correlations lead to unique azimuthal asymmetries in inclusive -dihadron pair production and in back-to-back hadron pairs ( ), which are absent in the SM. Using published Belle and BaBar measurements together with projected sensitivities based on ratios of azimuthal asymmetries, we demonstrate that these measurements provide significant constraints on light-quark dipole couplings, with a reduced dependence on poorly known nonperturbative fragmentation functions and free from contamination by other new physics effects. This approach offers a clean and novel probe of light-quark dipole interactions in collider experiments.
tldr: This paper proposes using spin correlations in entangled quark pairs produced at lepton colliders to probe light-quark electromagnetic dipole moments, with constraints from Belle and BaBar data.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a clean and novel probe of light-quark dipole interactions, which are poorly constrained and could indicate new physics beyond the Standard Model.
method: They analyze spin correlations in quark-antiquark pairs produced at lepton colliders, which lead to azimuthal asymmetries in dihadron production. They use published Belle and BaBar measurements and projected sensitivities to constrain dipole couplings.
result: The measurements provide significant constraints on light-quark dipole couplings, with reduced dependence on fragmentation functions and free from contamination by other new physics effects.
conclusion: This approach offers a clean and novel probe of light-quark dipole interactions in collider experiments.

title: El Agente Cuántico: Automating Quantum Simulations
authors: Ignacio Gustin, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Juan B Pérez-Sánchez, Chris Crebolder, Jérôme F Gonthier, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Yuma Nakamura, Karthik Panicker, Manav Ramprasad, Aiwei Yin, Zijian Zhang, Yunheng Zou, Varinia Bernales And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract: Quantum simulation is central to understanding and designing quantum systems across physics and chemistry. However, its practical use is often limited by the exponential growth of Hilbert space and by the increasing complexity of modern quantum-simulation software. Here we introduce El Agente Cuántico, a multi-agent AI system that automates quantum-simulation workflows by translating natural-language scientific intent into executed and validated computations across heterogeneous quantum-software frameworks. By reasoning directly over library documentation and APIs, our agentic system dynamically assembles end-to-end simulations spanning—but not limited to—state preparation, closed- and open-system dynamics, tensor-network methods, quantum control, quantum error correction, and quantum resource estimation. The developed system unifies traditionally distinct simulation paradigms behind a single natural-language interface. Beyond reducing technical barriers, this approach opens a path toward scalable, adaptive, and increasingly autonomous quantum simulation, enabling faster exploration of physical models, rapid hypothesis testing, and closer integration between theory, simulation, and emerging quantum hardware.
tldr: This paper introduces an AI agent system for automating quantum simulations via natural language, but it does not align with the specified research directions.
motivation: Quantum simulation is limited by complexity and software heterogeneity; the authors aim to lower barriers and accelerate research.
method: They develop a multi-agent AI system that interprets natural language, reasons over documentation and APIs, and assembles end-to-end simulations across various quantum software frameworks.
result: The system unifies different simulation paradigms behind a single interface, enabling automated state preparation, dynamics, tensor networks, control, error correction, and resource estimation.
conclusion: This approach could make quantum simulation more accessible and adaptive, but it is not a core contribution to the listed research areas.

title: From Intuition To Optimization: A Review Of Inverse Design Applied To Optical Nanotweezers
authors: Sejeong Kim And Kenneth B Crozier Damian Nelson
abstract: Optical nanotweezers, which integrate nanophotonic structures such as plasmonic antennas, dielectric resonators, and metasurfaces, have emerged as powerful tools for manipulating nanoparticles, biomolecules, and viruses with high precision. However, traditional designs rely heavily on heuristic approaches and simple geometries, limiting performance. Inverse design offers a paradigm shift by using computational optimization methods to discover non-intuitive, high-performance structures for optical trapping. This review provides an overview of key inverse design methodologies, including adjoint-based optimization, topology optimization, and machine learning approaches, and highlights their broader impact across nanophotonics. We then focus on their application to optical nanotweezers, where recent advances demonstrate enhanced trapping stiffness, reduced optical heating, and tailored trapping landscapes. Representative examples include algorithmic design of plasmonic nanotweezers, topology-optimized plasmonic nanoapertures, inverse-designed dielectric nanocavities, and force-centric designs based on Maxwell stress tensor engineering. Collectively, these studies illustrate how inverse design enables stable, efficient, and versatile optical trapping at the nanoscale. Despite these advances, challenges remain in fabrication, computational cost, and the interpretability of optimized structures. We conclude with a perspective on future directions, emphasizing opportunities in reconfigurable tweezers, lab-on-a-chip integration, and quantum nanophotonics. By bridging photonic optimization with nanoscale manipulation, inverse-designed optical nanotweezers offer promising opportunities for future applications in biophysics, materials science, and quantum technologies.
tldr: This review covers inverse design methods for optical nanotweezers, focusing on nanophotonic optimization for trapping, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize recent advances in inverse design for optical nanotweezers, which are used for manipulating nanoparticles and biomolecules, but the topic is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The review discusses adjoint-based optimization, topology optimization, and machine learning approaches applied to optical nanotweezers, including plasmonic and dielectric designs.
result: The paper highlights enhanced trapping stiffness, reduced heating, and tailored trapping landscapes, but these results are in the context of nanophotonics and biophysics, not quantum information processing.
conclusion: The authors conclude with future directions in reconfigurable tweezers and lab-on-a-chip integration, but the work does not contribute to the user's specified research areas.

title: Review For Stokes-vector And Mueller-matrix Polarization Imaging Technology: Principles, Implementation And Applications
authors: Nan Wang, Houxin Fan, Quanzhou Long And Sailing He
abstract: This review systematically summarizes the principles, technological advancements, and diverse applications of Stokes-vector and Mueller-matrix polarization imaging (PI). The polarization of light is a fundamental property that provides unique and valuable information about the interaction between light and matter. While traditional polarimetry is limited to point-by-point measurements, PI captures the polarization state in a two-dimensional scene, generating a spatial map of parameters for complex and heterogeneous systems. The Stokes–Mueller formalism is the only complete mathematical tool for polarization analysis, using the Stokes vector to describe the light’s state and the Mueller matrix as the transfer function to fully characterize the polarization-altering properties of any medium, including complex depolarizing tissues. The evolution of PI from time-sequential to snapshot paradigms represents a pivotal shift, driven by the pressing need for real-time, motion-artifact-free characterization of dynamic systems. While time-sequential systems laid the foundational framework, their inherent trade-off between acquisition speed and polarization completeness has spurred intense innovation in snapshot methodologies. This transition is not merely a technical improvement but a fundamental enabler for applying polarization analysis to in vivo biological processes and real-time industrial inspection. Applications of PI are wide-ranging, including label-free diagnostics for cancer detection, non-destructive analysis of anisotropic materials, polarization-enhanced target detection, and so on. A future direction is the convergence of PI with hyperspectral detection to form ‘hyper-Stokes/Mueller imaging,’ which promises unprecedented specificity and real-time capability.

result: The review outlines the transition to snapshot imaging for real-time applications and discusses future convergence with hyperspectral imaging.
conclusion: Polarization imaging is a versatile tool for label-free diagnostics and material analysis, with future potential in hyper-spectral combined systems.
